### Introduction

Here we are working on our second project for ST 558, back to the old grindstone... We will work on building a shiny app to allow a user to explore a data set of our choosing.

For this project, I decided to use player-level data from the 2025-2026 UEFA Champions League (UCL) season (highest level of professional soccer) to build my app (Source: FotMob). The criteria for a player being included in the data set is that they had to make at least 1 appearance (as either a starter or a substitute) in the UCL season at any point.

Let's start by downloading the data into our session:

```{r Libs}

library(utils)
library(tidyverse)
library(gt)

```

### Download Data

We are pulling in 2 separate data sets below:

1) Player Matches: This data set contains match-level information from our 2025-26 UCL season for each player that registered at least 1 appearance. This includes information like player rating, minutes played, goals scored, expected goals, etc. 

2) Player Season: This data set contains season-level information from our UCL season for each player that registered at least 1 appearance. This includes information like total number of goals, total minutes played, expected goals per 90 minutes, etc. 


```{r Pull data}

player_matches <- read.csv("data/player_matches.csv")
player_season <- read.csv("data/player_season.csv")

```

## Static Exploration

Let's start light with some 1-way contingency tables to explore our data. Personally, I am a fan of Borussia Dortmund, who are a German Club in the Bundesliga, which is the highest division in German professional soccer. I am interested in the number of appearances, number of goals, and number of assists held by every player on the team:

```{r Dortmund 1-way CT}

#Number of Appearances
gt(player_matches |>
  filter(team_name == "Borussia Dortmund") |>
  group_by(player_name) |>
  summarize(Appearances = n()) |>
  arrange(desc(Appearances))) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Number of Appearances - Borussia Dortmund",
    subtitle = "2025-26 UEFA Champions League"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    player_name = "Player"
  )

#Total number of goals scored
gt(player_matches |>
  filter(team_name == "Borussia Dortmund") |>
  group_by(player_name) |>
  summarize(Goals = sum(goals__value)) |>
  arrange(desc(Goals))) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Number of Goals Scored - Borussia Dortmund",
    subtitle = "2025-26 UEFA Champions League"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    player_name = "Player"
  )
  

#Total number of assists
gt(player_matches |>
  filter(team_name == "Borussia Dortmund") |>
  group_by(player_name) |>
  summarize(Assists = sum(assists__value)) |>
  arrange(desc(Assists))) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Number of Assists - Borussia Dortmund",
    subtitle = "2025-26 UEFA Champions League"
  ) |>
  cols_label(
    player_name = "Player"
  )

```

Now let's take a look at the same metrics, but add another layer of detail and see whether or not the players were starters or substitutes:

```{r Dortmund 2-way CT}

#Number of Appearances
gt(player_matches |>
  filter(team_name == "Borussia Dortmund") |>
  mutate(starter = if_else(starter == "True", "Starter", "Substitute")) |>
  group_by(player_name, starter) |>
  summarize(Appearances = n()) |>
  arrange(desc(Appearances)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = starter, values_from = Appearances) |>
  mutate(Starter = coalesce(Starter, 0), Substitute = coalesce(Substitute, 0))
) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Number of Appearances by Appearance Type - Borussia Dortmund",
    subtitle = "2025-26 UEFA Champions League"
  )  

#Total number of goals scored
gt(player_matches |>
  filter(team_name == "Borussia Dortmund") |>
  mutate(starter = if_else(starter == "True", "Starter", "Substitute")) |>
  group_by(player_name, starter) |>
  summarize(Total_Goals = sum(goals__value)) |>
  arrange(desc(Total_Goals)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = starter, values_from = Total_Goals) |>
  mutate(Starter = coalesce(Starter, 0), Substitute = coalesce(Substitute, 0))
) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Number of Goals by Appearance Type - Borussia Dortmund",
    subtitle = "2025-26 UEFA Champions League"
  ) 


#Total number of assists
gt(player_matches |>
  filter(team_name == "Borussia Dortmund") |>
  mutate(starter = if_else(starter == "True", "Starter", "Substitute")) |>
  group_by(player_name, starter) |>
  summarize(Total_Assists = sum(assists__value)) |>
  arrange(desc(Total_Assists)) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = starter, values_from = Total_Assists) |>
  mutate(Starter = coalesce(Starter, 0), Substitute = coalesce(Substitute, 0))
) |>
  tab_header(
    title = "Number of Assists by Appearance Type - Borussia Dortmund",
    subtitle = "2025-26 UEFA Champions League"
  ) 

```

To be honest, these goal and assist numbers don't look too hot for a Top-Flight German team that is (supposedly) meant to be a top 2 team in Germany, and a top 12 club in Europe. Luckily, out data (and many other sources of soccer data), track player match ratings for each game, which scale from 1-10. In the FotMob rating system, each player starts their appearance with a 6.0 rating, which increases or decreases based on their actions during the game.
